<!-- slide 195 -->
# Pathway Enrichment {.divider}

[From gene list to biology · Day 01]{.eyebrow}


<!-- slide 196 -->
## What Enrichment Asks {.smaller}

[Pathway enrichment · theory]{.eyebrow}

### Is any pathway over-represented in my gene list?

You ran differential expression, you have a list of significant genes. Enrichment asks: do those genes fall into known pathways (GO terms, KEGG) **more than chance**? A pathway with 5 of your 50 genes when the genome would predict 1 is enriched, evidence that process is involved.

The workflow is always the same: **DE → significant genes → test each pathway against a background → rank by adjusted p-value → plot the top hits**. The fixing-up is multiple testing: you test thousands of pathways, so you read `p_adj`, not raw p.


<!-- slide 197 -->
## Getting Enrichment · gget {.smaller}

[Pathway enrichment · the tool]{.eyebrow}

### One call to the Enrichr database

`gget enrichr` takes a gene list and a library name and returns a ranked table, no account, no upload. It hits a web API, so we ran it once and saved the result into `load_enrichment()`; the deck plots that offline.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# pip install gget   (this call needs internet — we pre-saved its output)
import gget

drought_genes = ["RD29A", "DREB2A", "ABA1", "NCED3", "P5CS1",   # your significant genes
                 "RAB18", "COR15A", "LEA14", "RD22", "ERD10"]
res = gget.enrichr(drought_genes, database="GO_Biological_Process_2021")

# res columns include: path_name, adj_p_val, overlapping_genes
res[["path_name", "adj_p_val", "overlapping_genes"]].head()
# → we cleaned this into load_enrichment(): pathway, direction, p_adj, gene_count, gene_ratio
```


<!-- slide 198 -->
## Pathway · The Data {.smaller}

[Pathway enrichment]{.eyebrow}

### The pre-computed results table

`load_enrichment()` holds the enriched pathways for both directions: each pathway, its adjusted p-value, how many of your genes hit it (`gene_count`), the fraction of the pathway you hit (`gene_ratio`), and a functional `category`.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column
from genomics_course.data import load_enrichment

en = load_enrichment()   # pathway, direction, p_adj, gene_count, gene_ratio, category
en.head(4)
```


<!-- slide 199 -->
## Pathway Bars · Step 1 — Rank by Significance {.smaller}

[Pathway enrichment · build]{.eyebrow}

### 1 · −log10(p), sorted into bars

p-values are tiny and uneven, so transform to `−log10(p_adj)`: bigger = more significant. Sort and draw horizontal bars so the long labels stay readable.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "4,6-8"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 5.0
from genomics_course.data import load_enrichment

en = load_enrichment()                                   # pathway, direction, p_adj, ...
en["nlp"] = -np.log10(en.p_adj)                          # significance on a readable scale
d = en.sort_values("nlp")                                # smallest at bottom

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 5.0))
ax.barh(range(len(d)), d.nlp, color=GREY)                # one bar per pathway
ax.set_yticks(range(len(d))); ax.set_yticklabels(d.pathway, fontsize=7.5)
ax.set_xlabel("−log₁₀(adjusted p)")
for s in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 200 -->
## Pathway Bars · Step 2 — Colour by Direction {.smaller}

[Pathway enrichment · build]{.eyebrow}

### 2 · Induced vs repressed

Map a colour to each regulation direction. Now you can see whether drought-induced pathways differ in kind from the repressed ones, they do.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "5,9"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 5.0
from genomics_course.data import load_enrichment

en = load_enrichment()
en["nlp"] = -np.log10(en.p_adj)
d = en.sort_values("nlp")
dir_pal = {"up": GREEN, "down": BLUE}                    # induced vs repressed

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 5.0))
ax.barh(range(len(d)), d.nlp, color=d.direction.map(dir_pal), alpha=.9)  # colour each bar
ax.set_yticks(range(len(d))); ax.set_yticklabels(d.pathway, fontsize=7.5)
ax.set_xlabel("−log₁₀(adjusted p)")
for s in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 201 -->
## Pathway Bars · Step 3 — Threshold & Finding {.smaller}

[Pathway enrichment · build]{.eyebrow}

### 3 · Mark significance, name the biology

Add a dashed line at `p = 0.05` (everything right of it is significant), a legend, and a title that states the result. The split is clean: stress and signalling up, photosynthesis and growth down.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "11,14-16,17-18"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 5.0
from genomics_course.data import load_enrichment
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D                      # for the legend swatches

en = load_enrichment()
en["nlp"] = -np.log10(en.p_adj)
d = en.sort_values("nlp")
dir_pal = {"up": GREEN, "down": BLUE}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 5.0))
ax.barh(range(len(d)), d.nlp, color=d.direction.map(dir_pal), alpha=.9)
ax.axvline(-np.log10(0.05), color=RED, ls="--", lw=1.1)  # significance threshold
ax.set_yticks(range(len(d))); ax.set_yticklabels(d.pathway, fontsize=7.5)
ax.set_xlabel("−log₁₀(adjusted p)")
for s in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
handles = [Line2D([0], [0], marker="s", color="w", markerfacecolor=c, label=k, ms=8)
           for k, c in dir_pal.items()]                  # up / down key
ax.legend(handles=handles, frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="lower right")
ax.set_title("DROUGHT INDUCES STRESS, REPRESSES PHOTOSYNTHESIS",
             color="#333333", fontweight="bold", fontsize=9, loc="left")
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 202 -->
## Pathway Bubbles · Step 1 — Add Two More Variables {.smaller}

[Pathway enrichment · build]{.eyebrow}

### 1 · Gene ratio on x, count as size

A bar shows one number; a bubble shows three. Put `gene_ratio` on the x-axis and scale each marker by `gene_count`, so a big bubble far right is a pathway you hit broadly and deeply.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "5-7"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 5.0
from genomics_course.data import load_enrichment

en = load_enrichment()
en["nlp"] = -np.log10(en.p_adj)
top = en.nlargest(10, "nlp").sort_values("nlp")          # ten most significant

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 5.0))
ax.scatter(top.gene_ratio, range(len(top)),              # x = ratio, y = pathway
           s=top.gene_count * 6, color=GREY, alpha=.8)   # bubble size = gene count
ax.set_yticks(range(len(top))); ax.set_yticklabels(top.pathway, fontsize=7.5)
ax.set_xlabel("gene ratio (hits / pathway size)")
for s in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```


<!-- slide 203 -->
## Pathway Bubbles · Step 2 — Colour by Category {.smaller}

[Pathway enrichment · build]{.eyebrow}

### 2 · A fourth variable: function

Colour the bubbles by functional `category` and add a legend. Four dimensions, significance (rank), breadth (x), size (count), and function (colour), on one panel.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-line-numbers: "5,9,13-15"
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 5.0
from genomics_course.data import load_enrichment
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

en = load_enrichment()
en["nlp"] = -np.log10(en.p_adj)
top = en.nlargest(10, "nlp").sort_values("nlp")
cat_pal = {"Stress": RED, "Signaling": AMBER, "Metabolism": PURPLE,   # colour per function
           "Photosynthesis": GREEN, "Growth": BLUE}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 5.0))
ax.scatter(top.gene_ratio, range(len(top)), s=top.gene_count * 6,
           c=top.category.map(cat_pal), alpha=.8, linewidths=0)   # colour by category
ax.set_yticks(range(len(top))); ax.set_yticklabels(top.pathway, fontsize=7.5)
ax.set_xlabel("gene ratio (hits / pathway size)")
for s in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
handles = [Line2D([0], [0], marker="o", color="w", markerfacecolor=c, label=k, ms=8)
           for k, c in cat_pal.items()]
ax.legend(handles=handles, frameon=False, fontsize=7, title="category", loc="lower right")
plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
[The bottom line]{.tl}
Enrichment turns a gene list into ranked biology: **`gget enrichr` to get the table → −log10(p) bars to rank → bubbles to add gene ratio, count, and function**. Read `p_adj`, not raw p, and always show how many genes drove each hit.
:::


<!-- slide 204 -->
## Exercise · Read the Enrichment {.smaller}

[Pathway enrichment · exercise]{.eyebrow}

### Which pathways, and how confident?

::: {.exercise}
[Real scenario]{.xl}
A reviewer asks: of the drought-**induced** pathways, which clear significance, and which is supported by the most of your genes? Filter `load_enrichment()` and rank two ways.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
from genomics_course.data import load_enrichment

en = load_enrichment()                          # pathway, direction, p_adj, gene_count, ...

# 1. keep only direction == "up"
# 2. significant?  en.p_adj < 0.05
# 3. most significant:    sort by p_adj ascending, take top 3
# 4. best-supported:      sort by gene_count descending, take top 3
# 5. do the two top-3 lists agree? (low p and high gene_count aren't the same thing)
```
:::
